name: Potion Ratio Lab
mechanic: The recipe card says a ratio (e.g. 2 red drops for every 1 blue). The child drags drops into the cauldron to MATCH that ratio across a larger batch (4 red + 2 blue). Pour wrong, the potion fizzles gray; pour the right ratio and it transforms into a glowing color with a poof.
why_distinct: Magic-machine is single input->funnel->one output; this is a RATIO transform where the CONFIGURATION (relative amounts) encodes the answer, not a count. Closest neighbor is my recipe-double-02; separation: this matches a fixed proportion within one batch, recipe-double scales a whole recipe up/down by a factor.
fun_no_competition: The cauldron bubbles, smokes the wrong color when off, then erupts in sparkling correct color — the surprise transform IS the reward.
character_world: A clumsy wizard-frog's potion shop where every brew makes a different silly creature appear
web_shell_feasibility: feasible — DOM drop counters + CSS color blend + sprite-sheet poof animation
asset_idea: stub: colored circle drops + gray cauldron PNG. CA5: cauldron 6-frame bubble loop, fizzle-gray poof sequence, glow-color success poof, wizard-frog reaction sprites

name: Recipe Double & Half
mechanic: A recipe lists ingredient amounts for 2 cupcakes. A sign flips to 'Make 4!' (double) or 'Make 1!' (half). The child taps each ingredient up or down to the correct doubled/halved amount, then the oven bakes — correct amounts yield perfect cupcakes, wrong yields a lopsided one.
why_distinct: Not magic-machine's one-op-one-output: this transforms an ENTIRE SET of quantities by the same scalar (doubling/halving each line). Closest neighbor potion-ratio-01; separation: ratio-lab matches a proportion in one batch, this applies x2 or /2 to every ingredient simultaneously (operate, not match).
fun_no_competition: The oven dings and reveals a tray of identical perfect cupcakes (or one comically melted one) — predicting the bake outcome is the joy.
character_world: A bakery run by a tiny mouse chef who narrates each bake with delight
web_shell_feasibility: feasible — DOM steppers + oven sprite reveal
asset_idea: stub: ingredient icons + number steppers. CA5: oven door open/close, perfect cupcake tray + lopsided fail variant, mouse-chef cheer/oops sprites

name: Domino Chain Setup
mechanic: Empty slots sit between a START button and a GOAL bell. The child drags dominoes into the slots so that when triggered, the falling chain reaches the bell. The skill is COUNTING the gap and placing exactly enough dominoes (e.g. 6 slots need 6 dominoes); the child sets it up, then taps START to watch the chain fall.
why_distinct: Set-up-then-trigger where the SETUP encodes the answer — distinct from path-journey (which is moving along a route) because nothing moves until the child triggers it and the configuration must be COMPLETE-and-correct first. Closest neighbor marble-run-09; separation: dominoes is straight-line count-to-fill, marble-run is branching path-choice.
fun_no_competition: The whole row topples in a satisfying clack-clack-clack and rings the bell — watching your setup cascade is the payoff.
character_world: A cheerful robot's domino workshop where the bell wakes a sleeping cat
web_shell_feasibility: feasible — DOM slot placement + CSS sequential tip animation
asset_idea: stub: rectangle dominoes + bell PNG. CA5: domino tip-over frames, bell ring + cat-wake sprite, robot encourage poses

name: Grow & Shrink Ray
mechanic: A creature stands at a number on a number line. The ray gun shows '+3' or '-2'. The child PREDICTS where the creature lands by tapping the target spot on the line, then fires — the ray zaps and the creature jumps that many, growing/shrinking as it goes. Land it right, it cheers from the correct spot.
why_distinct: A transform applied along a NUMBER LINE where the child predicts the result-position before triggering. Closest neighbor word-morph-13; separation: that morphs letters via rules, this transforms a position by add/subtract on a numeric line (math, not spelling).
fun_no_competition: The zap noise + the creature ballooning bigger or squishing smaller as it hops — predicting where it lands and being right is delightful.
character_world: A mad-but-kind inventor zapping bouncy blobs in a lab
web_shell_feasibility: feasible — DOM number line + CSS scale transform + hop animation
asset_idea: stub: blob at line tick + ray-gun. CA5: ray beam frames, blob grow/shrink squash-stretch sequence, inventor sprites

name: Ice-to-Water Melt Meter
mechanic: An ice block sits under a sun-lamp dial. The child turns the heat dial and watches the ice melt through stages (solid -> dripping -> puddle -> steam). Prompts ask the child to set the dial to the stage that matches a described state ('make it a liquid'). Setting the right heat triggers the matching transform.
why_distinct: A continuous reversible STATE transform (solid/liquid/gas) controlled by a dial — not magic-machine's discrete one-shot. Closest neighbor weather-machine-12; separation: weather-machine sequences cause->effect events, this is a single substance morphing through ordered states by one control.
fun_no_competition: Watching ice slowly drip then puff into steam, and being able to crank it back to ice — the reversible morph is mesmerizing.
character_world: A penguin scientist studying its melting ice cube with worried curiosity
web_shell_feasibility: feasible — DOM dial + CSS opacity/shape crossfade between state PNGs
asset_idea: stub: ice cube + heat dial. CA5: 4-stage melt sequence (ice->drip->puddle->steam), penguin reaction sprites

name: Combine & Split Blobs
mechanic: Two blobs of given sizes (numbers) sit on a fusion pad. The prompt asks to COMBINE them ('put 3 and 2 together') — child drags them onto the pad and they merge into one blob; the child taps the keypad with the new total to confirm. Or it asks to SPLIT a big blob into two named parts.
why_distinct: Physical combine/split as the literal transform of addition/decomposition — the blobs MERGE or DIVIDE visually. Closest neighbor grow-shrink-04; separation: that moves one creature on a line, this fuses/separates two whole objects into one or vice versa (part-whole, not position).
fun_no_competition: Two googly blobs squish into one wobbly bigger blob with a 'sploot' — or a big one pinches into two — pure transform satisfaction.
character_world: A gooey-blob playground where blobs giggle when they merge
web_shell_feasibility: feasible — DOM blob elements + CSS merge/split keyframes
asset_idea: stub: two sized circle blobs + fusion pad. CA5: merge squish frames, split pinch frames, blob faces

name: Word Plus-S Machine
mechanic: A single object (one cat) goes in a conveyor. The child sees the word 'cat' and the prompt makes MORE of them (3 cats appear). The child must transform the word by adding the right ending — tapping the '+s' stamp to make 'cats' — and the machine only releases the correct plural that matches the picture count.
why_distinct: A WORD transform (singular->plural) triggered by a stamp, with the picture-count as the cause. Distinct from story-maker (assembling sentences) — here one word morphs by an inflection rule. Closest neighbor word-morph-13; separation: that swaps letters to make a new word, this appends a grammatical ending matched to quantity.
fun_no_competition: The +s stamp THUNKS down and an extra letter pops on with a sparkle, then the right number of critters tumble out — the matching morph delights.
character_world: A copy-machine factory run by a tidy raccoon who stamps words
web_shell_feasibility: feasible — DOM letter tiles + stamp animation + critter sprites
asset_idea: stub: word tiles + +s stamp + critter PNGs. CA5: stamp thunk frames, sparkle on new letter, raccoon operator sprites

name: Rube-Goldberg Trigger Builder
mechanic: A scene has 3 broken gaps in a chain (a missing ramp, a missing bucket, a missing fan). The child drags the correct piece into each gap from a tray, ORDERED first-to-last as the prompt narrates ('first the ball rolls, next it...'). Once all gaps are filled correctly, tapping GO runs the whole contraption.
why_distinct: Multi-step cause-effect CHAIN where the child completes a sequence of triggers — distinct from domino-03 (homogeneous count) because each piece is a DIFFERENT mechanism and ORDER/role matters. Sequencing is the skill (first/next/last).
fun_no_competition: The full contraption fires in a chain — ball rolls, fan blows, balloon pops confetti — watching your assembled sequence run end-to-end is the joy.
character_world: A bumbling cat-engineer's invention to wake a snoozing hamster
web_shell_feasibility: feasible — DOM gap slots + CSS sequential trigger animation chain
asset_idea: stub: ramp/bucket/fan pieces + scene. CA5: per-mechanism action frames, final confetti pop, cat-engineer reactions

name: Marble Run Branch Picker
mechanic: A marble drops from the top of a track with FORKS. At each fork the child taps a flipper to set its direction so the marble reaches the labeled goal bin. The child sets ALL flippers first (planning the path), then releases the marble to see it bounce through the configuration.
why_distinct: Set-up-then-trigger with BRANCHING choices encoding a route — distinct from path-journey (you move step by step) because the child pre-configures every fork then watches a single physics-like drop. Closest neighbor domino-03; separation: dominoes is linear count, this is branch-direction logic.
fun_no_competition: The marble pings down through every flipper you set and plops into the right bin — predicting the path and nailing it is the delight.
character_world: A squirrel's acorn-sorting marble machine in a treehouse
web_shell_feasibility: feasible — DOM track + flipper toggles + CSS marble drop animation
asset_idea: stub: track with forks + flippers + bins. CA5: marble bounce frames, flipper flip, squirrel cheer sprites

name: Weather Machine Cause-Effect
mechanic: A control panel has cause buttons (Sun, Rain, Wind, Cold). A scene shows a plant/puddle/snowman. The prompt states a desired EFFECT ('make the puddle disappear') and the child must press the cause that produces it (Sun -> puddle evaporates). Pressing the wrong cause shows a silly mismatch and asks again.
why_distinct: Pure cause->effect reasoning: pick the input that yields the stated outcome. Distinct from melt-meter-05 (one dial, one substance through states) because here multiple DIFFERENT causes map to different effects on different objects. Closest neighbor rube-goldberg-08; separation: that orders a chain, this is single cause->effect matching.
fun_no_competition: Press Rain and a flower blooms; press Cold and the puddle freezes solid — the immediate transform reaction is the whole fun.
character_world: A friendly cloud-creature operating a backyard weather console
web_shell_feasibility: feasible — DOM buttons + CSS scene-state swaps + sprite reactions
asset_idea: stub: weather buttons + scene objects. CA5: per-effect transform sequences (bloom, evaporate, freeze, blow), cloud-creature sprites

name: Tens-Frame Carry Machine
mechanic: A loose-ones bin fills as the child taps to add ones. When it hits 10, the machine AUTO-BUNDLES them into a ten-rod with a satisfying clunk and carries it to the tens column. The child works toward a target number, watching ten ones transform into one ten each time the bin fills.
why_distinct: A transform that fires on a THRESHOLD (ten ones -> one ten) — the cause is reaching capacity, the effect is regrouping. Distinct from combine-split-06 (free merge of two blobs) because this is a place-value bundling triggered automatically at 10. Closest neighbor blob-combine; separation: threshold-bundling vs arbitrary fusion.
fun_no_competition: The bin fills, glows, and CLUNKS ten loose ones into a tidy ten-rod that slides over — the auto-bundle transform is deeply satisfying.
character_world: A factory-robot that loves tidying loose blocks into neat bundles
web_shell_feasibility: feasible — DOM unit cubes + CSS bundle-collapse animation + place-value columns
asset_idea: stub: unit cubes + bin + ten-rod. CA5: 10-cubes-collapse-to-rod frames, slide-over, robot happy sprites

name: Seed-to-Bloom Time Crank
mechanic: A seed sits in soil with a time-crank handle. The child turns the crank and watches the plant grow through ordered stages (seed -> sprout -> bud -> bloom). The prompt names a stage and the child cranks to exactly that stage. Over-cranking wilts it (and they can crank back), teaching the ordered sequence.
why_distinct: A reversible ORDERED-STAGE transform via a crank, focused on sequence/ordinal language. Distinct from melt-meter-05 (physical states of one substance) — this is biological GROWTH stages and targets ordinal sequencing. Closest neighbor melt-meter; separation: grow-stages teach first/next/last ordering, melt teaches states.
fun_no_competition: Cranking the handle and watching the plant unfurl leaf by leaf, then bloom — and rewinding it back to a seed — is pure transform wonder.
character_world: A gentle bug-gardener narrating its plant's growth
web_shell_feasibility: feasible — DOM crank slider + CSS stage crossfade
asset_idea: stub: soil + crank + plant stages. CA5: seed->sprout->bud->bloom sequence + wilt frame, bug-gardener sprites

name: Letter-Swap Morph Lab
mechanic: A word sits in a chamber (cat). The prompt says 'change one sound to make CAP' or 'swap the first letter to make HAT'. The child drags the new letter into the right slot; the machine zaps and the word MORPHS, then a picture of the new word appears. One-letter-at-a-time transformation chains words.
why_distinct: A WORD-CHAIN transform: change one phoneme/letter to morph into a new word, with each step a real word. Distinct from plus-s-07 (append a grammatical ending) because here you SWAP a sound within the word (phonemic substitution). Distinct from build-a-word entirely — the chamber transforms an existing word.
fun_no_competition: The zap, the letter spinning into place, and the picture flipping from a cat to a hat — watching one swap morph the whole word is magic.
character_world: A word-wizard owl in a glowing transformation chamber
web_shell_feasibility: feasible — DOM letter slots + CSS zap + picture swap
asset_idea: stub: word chamber + letter tiles + result pictures. CA5: zap morph frames, picture cross-swap, owl-wizard sprites

name: Mixing Color Predictor
mechanic: Two paint pumps (e.g. blue + yellow) feed a mixer. Before mixing, the child PREDICTS the result by tapping the swatch they think it makes (green), then pulls the lever — the paints swirl and pour out the actual color. The prompt drives which mixes to do; matching the prediction is the goal.
why_distinct: Predict-then-trigger where two inputs COMBINE into an emergent third (color mixing) — the prediction is the answer, the trigger reveals it. Distinct from potion-ratio-01 (proportion matching) because mixing is qualitative combination (which color results), not quantity. Closest neighbor combine-split-06; separation: blobs combine sizes (number), this combines properties (color).
fun_no_competition: The two paints swirl together and gush out a brand-new color — guessing it first and watching it pour confirms the surprise.
character_world: A messy-but-happy octopus painter at a color-mixing organ
web_shell_feasibility: feasible — DOM pumps + CSS swirl + color blend output
asset_idea: stub: paint pumps + mixer + swatches. CA5: paint swirl frames, color pour, octopus splat reactions

name: Shape-Fold Transformer
mechanic: A flat 2D shape (square, triangle pattern) sits on a folding table. The prompt asks 'fold this to make a cube/cone'. The child taps fold lines in sequence and the net animates folding up into the 3D shape. Choosing the right net + folds transforms flat into solid with a snap.
why_distinct: A geometric 2D->3D transform via folding — the cause (which folds) produces the solid. Distinct from marble-branch-09 (route logic) — this morphs a flat net into a named solid. Closest neighbor letter-swap-13 (a chamber morph) but operates on SHAPES not words and teaches 2D/3D relationships.
fun_no_competition: The flat paper creases and lifts into a real cube with a crisp snap — watching 2D pop into 3D is a tiny delightful miracle.
character_world: An origami-fox who folds flat scraps into pop-up creatures
web_shell_feasibility: needs-richer-runtime — true 3D fold animation is hard in pure DOM/CSS; feasible with pre-rendered CA5 fold sprite-sheets per net rather than live 3D
asset_idea: stub: flat net + fold-line buttons + solid result. CA5: per-net fold-up sequence sprite-sheets, snap pop, origami-fox sprites

name: Syllable Stretch & Squish
mechanic: A word-creature on an accordion stretches when the child pulls it apart, splitting into syllable chunks ('but-ter-fly' = 3 claps), or squishes back together. The prompt asks how many parts; the child stretches it into exactly that many chunks and each chunk lights+sounds as it separates.
why_distinct: A physical STRETCH/SQUISH transform of a word into syllable chunks — reversible, tactile. Distinct from letter-swap-13 (substitution) and plus-s-07 (append) because it SEGMENTS one word into parts via stretching. The accordion physical metaphor for syllabification is the novel core.
fun_no_competition: Pulling the word apart like taffy and hearing each chunk pop, then snapping it back together — the stretch-and-pop transform is tactile fun.
character_world: A stretchy-worm word-creature that giggles when pulled into pieces
web_shell_feasibility: feasible — DOM accordion stretch via transform + per-chunk highlight + TTS per syllable
asset_idea: stub: word on accordion band + chunk segments. CA5: stretch-apart frames, chunk glow, squish-back, worm-creature faces
